source: Rosie, please be careful. The King has set up a terrible plot involving you, Guildenstern, and Hamlet.
A plot? Of what sort?
He gave you a letter, did he not?
Yes, but...
There's something awful in that letter, isn't there?
Hamlet will find it soon, if he hasn't already. He'll believe you mean him harm.
...Well, now that I know of it, that's neither here nor there.
I wouldn't hand over any such letter like that. Now that you've tipped me off, it shan't be a problem.
But Guilda would be crushed. She'd never want any harm to come to Hamlet.
If you decide to tell her this news, please do it gently, Ophelia.
If he hasn't told you already, he means to send you and Guilda to England with Hamlet.
...And he'll hand you a letter.
A letter? Saying what, precisely?
That his uncle means to have him executed upon arrival.
Ah, no, you must be mistaken. The King denied Hamlet's request to leave Denmark.
Although, come to think of it, Guildenstern would be overjoyed if such a thing occurred.
(Ah, right. Claudius hasn't hatched a plan to send Hamlet away just yet.)
I found a note on your desk accusing Hamlet of stealing your lute. Can we talk about it?
It's been returned. The matter is resolved.
Hamlet-- and I-- we spoke honestly. For perhaps the first time in our lives.
I no longer desire his downfall. Whether I cheer for his success is another matter entirely.
Oh... oh, Ophelia. I left that as an idle thought for Father. I'm a bit occupied at the moment—I've got to make my departure soon.
When I return from Paris, we'll have endless time to hash through it. I promise.
No. I demanded Hamlet return what is mine.
If he's ready to bring my property back to me, then I'll speak with him further.
Until then, there's no reason to speak to him—or you.
Hamlet - your uncle is not your enemy. Peter Quince is.
Don't even speak to me of that idiot. He's gone and ruined everything.
I don't know why I ever trusted the man.
(...He's in a frenzy by now. It's too late.)
(If I'd caught him earlier...)
Peter Quince... the name's familiar...
Ah, that playmaster? What... can you mean, Ophelia?
I haven't seen the man in close to a decade, nor heard of him since.
He's going to arrive in Elsinore soon. I've... heard... word that he plans to put on a performance here.
Peter Quince the playmaster? What on earth do you mean?
I know it seems far-fetched, but please, listen to me carefully.
Quince is evil. He means to take down all of us.
Your father's death, your grandmother's insanity—it was all his doing. All of it.
He drove them insane from the shadows. He conspired to have them dead.
You are saying... my father was not murdered by my uncle after all?
But how can that be? My father's spirit spoke to me. I heard it say that Claudius was my father's killer.
Was the spirit some omen of the devil? Was I lied to?
No, Hamlet, you weren't lied to. It—it's hard to explain. He... conspired... to help your uncle kill your father.
These are cruel allegations to make without proof, Ophelia.
Then ask your father. Ask his ghost yourself. You know he appears on the walls at midnight.
(So long as I can convince the ghost of all this, he's the only one Hamlet will listen to...)
Your father will confirm everything I say. Please, Hamlet. If you don't believe me, no one else will.
And... then... I'll be out of options. He'll have won.
I don't know where else to turn.
Very well. Then let the visions of this night prove your words true.
And come, now. You know I can't stand it when you make faces like that. Everything will be all right, Ophelia. I'm here to help.
(I've got to make sure his father's spirit understands the situation we're in.)
My lord, Peter Quince means to bring dissent to the court. We should act against him.
That performance was truly horrid. Apologies for my reaction, but I simply couldn't tolerate it longer.
Nevertheless, it's come to my attention that my nephew was the one pulling the strings on that circumstance.
He means to do far more than that, my lord.
Oh? In what way?
It's... he'll... he sort of... manipulates people.
...You know, Ophelia, I'm rather busy at the moment.
Perhaps we might discuss your, er, theories at a later date.
Oh? The playmaster my wife invited? In what way?
It's hard to explain, but he's going to bring harm to you.
Father. Please believe me... Peter Quince intends to do you great harm.
Do you mean that funny little man the Queen invited to perform?
He's far more than that. I believe he intends to harm all of us.
Oh, my love—if you're worried, we'll have the guards watch after him more closely.
That won't be enough. We have to find a way to rid him from the castle.
Is everything all right, love? You've begun to sound an awful lot like... well...
Like Hamlet.
I think we're quite done with this discussion for now. You're worrying me.
My lady, I believe the Playmaster you invited means to sow dissent in the court.
He ought to be removed from the castle immediately.
Peter Quince? Why... but I just saw Hamlet speaking with him earlier.
I haven't seen my son so excited in quite some time.
What? That little man? He's only come to put on a frivolous play. And now, perhaps not even that.
How could he be sowing dissent, Ophelia?
...He... means to kill us all, my lady.
You included.
Laertes. Please listen to me. The Playmaster—Peter Quince—he intends to cause serious harm to us.
Who is that?
(Right. I'm too early.)
He's a performer. A loner. He often travels through Elsinore.
I know the one you mean, I think, though it's been years. I-- I see. So you believe he's trying to hurt someone?
In what way?
He's going to have you all killed.
A coup?
Yes! Yes, precisely! A coup of sorts—
Where are his men?
It's just him. But he has... strange... powers. Unearthly abilities.
Oh, no. I knew Hamlet was beginning to rub off on you.
Goodness, you gave me an honest fright. What a strange joke.
I met Simona, and she revealed to me the true culprit - Peter Quince, the playmaster, is behind us being trapped in Elsinore.
Yes. Hamlet, you, and I shall act anon.
A ghost, a mad prince, and... you. What a trio we shall be.
Peter Quince? He is but flesh and blood. What ill can he do to you?
I can assure you I had a conversation with him where he most certainly proved he was not human.
No. Impossible. Quince encouraged me to find the Book of Fates.
He urged me to find a way out using the Book as my guide...
Because he wanted it for himself. He tried to threaten me into handing it over. But I didn't give it to him.
For what purpose could he desire such an artifact?
Because he's trapped in this world--our world--until I use the Book of Fates and free us both. That's why he's been in Elsinore for so long.
Queen Astrid, you, me... none of us were able to use the Book and conclude his time in this world.
Until that happens, he'll only make new victims out of people in this castle.
He... and I... I've realized what this is. It's just like chess or cards. We're taking turns telling this story.
I do something, and then he bends the story in his favor. Simona told me the world would constantly spin towards disaster. She was right.
But I... can't figure out why. What does he get out of tormenting us? Of setting up these situations where everything devolves into blood?
And what's the point of it all if he's still trapped in this world regardless?
What? How?
Boredom can be quite frightening. Even I, who have been dead but a scarce several months, understand how frightening it is.
Unable to truly die, yet unable to engage with human life...
It is like standing outside a window, watching those inside gorge themselves on a feast. I press my hands against the glass nightly.
But try as I might, I cannot join them. I have relinquished my seat at that table, and a wolf now sits in my place.
Here I remain, bored out of my bones, lingering like refuse.
I-if that's true, then Quince is only... being cruel. Deeply, horribly cruel.
Yes. Cruelty is one cure for that boredom. A route I myself was inspired to take. And now my son wages revenge on my behalf.
You and Hamlet must speak. You must tell him. He'll only believe all this if he hears it from your mouth. It sounds insane otherwise.
And once you have, perhaps the three of us can find a way to stop Quince for good.
Agreed. You must bring my son to me.
Yes -- bring him here with those same words, and the three of us shall conspire to end Quince.
I did not understand when you brought him to me in this world. But now I do. Try once more, Ophelia.
I am aware.
He must be dealt with. But we cannot let him know of our plans.
What's the point of watching us suffer? Why? What does he get out of it?
I-if that's true, then he's... being cruel. Deeply, horribly cruel.
You won't succeed with this.
And what is 'this,' precisely?
Torturing me. Causing me to break down. I won't do it.
They all say that. Such a tired line.
Oh! Let me guess, your next line is—
'I'll never give up! I have the power... of heart!'
Lord, what fools these mortals be.
I don't think you'll ever see it my way.
Which is a shame, because I crave fresh dialogue.
Bernardo, I need you to help me protect the castle against Peter Quince.
Peter Quince? What's wrong?
He's going to have you all killed off.
Y-you wouldn't believe me if I told you. But he isn't human.
I know things have been rather rough as of late.
But please. Try to sleep more and take excellent care of your health. I worry for you.
You sound just like Hamlet. And right now, that is... perhaps... a liability of sorts.
Why were you rummaging around in odd places? What are you hiding?
Nothing. When I'm taken by surprise I sort of, ah, make strange noises.
Please don't tell anyone about what you saw. It'll be such an embarrassment to Guildenstern and me.
We weren't up to anything nefarious. I promise. Just errands for, ah, a friend. Hrrk...
Why were you rummaging around in odd places? What are you up to?
Hmm! Who wants ta' know?
Me. I want to know.
Well, it's a secret!
I witnessed Lady Rosencrantz and Guildenstern rummaging around in odd places. You were saying, about a spy...?
